source_review.notes: Checked current Azure Bulkhead guidance, AWS dependency-isolation guidance, Resilience4j Bulkhead behavior, Java SE 25 ThreadPoolExecutor/Semaphore specifications, current Kubernetes resource-management documentation and the cited reliability, distributed-systems, queueing and performance texts. Exact platform queue/fairness/isolation behavior remains version qualified.

evidence: Checked partition/resource indices, total capacity, reserve, allocation, in-flight, queue count/bytes, arrival/residence and lease-generation notation.
Checked per-resource allocation inequalities, Little's-Law estimate and admission/release conservation expressions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Resource dimensions remain separate; unused capacity in one cannot offset oversubscription in another.

evidence: Reproduced executable allocation 12+20+20+8=60, within total 60, and independent admission traces critical 2/3, standard 3/4 and batch 1/2.
Recomputed Exercise 2: available connections 84 versus 88 allocated (4 over); threads 72 versus 76 (4 over); memory 3,584 MiB versus 3,840 MiB (256 MiB over).
Recomputed Exercise 3 mean resident concurrency 180/s times 0.15 s = 27.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Mean concurrency and static counters do not choose tail-safe capacity or establish live isolation.

evidence: Verified atomic per-partition bounds plus allocation inequality conditionally bound tracked resource use.
Verified containment only when every resource required for protected progress is disjoint/reserved; any shared binding resource is a counterexample.
Verified unique lease acquisition/exactly-once release preserves available plus leased equals capacity and persistent arrival above service makes a finite queue eventually full.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Arguments exclude untracked consumers, capacity-estimation error, uncooperative work and residual shared resources.

evidence: Reviewed zero/exact/over limit, count versus bytes/age, permit acquisition before allocation, success/error/timeout/cancel/callback/shutdown release races and lingering physical work.
Reviewed hidden shared ingress, CPU, heap, GC, FD, connection, database lock/quota, DNS/identity/configuration/control-plane and cell/node/region resources.
Reviewed overpartitioning, hot tenant, strict priority/starvation, forged critical class, borrowing/nonpreemption, retry backoff, autoscaling, restart and safety-critical command/telemetry isolation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real driver, dependency, OS/container, fleet, security and safety containment requires integration/fault evidence and named review.

evidence: Traced failure-derived boundaries, finite resource vectors, per-resource budget fit, permit lifetime, explicit queue side and protected reserve through exposition/examples/answers.
Traced authenticated priority, bounded borrowing, downstream-aware scaling, residual dependency disclosure and protected-progress verification.
invariant_checking.notes: Rejection alone is never treated as proof that the protected class continues to succeed.

evidence: Reviewed static capacity, containment and release-conservation arguments against atomicity/tracking/disjointness premises.
Reviewed static-reserve versus borrowing utilization tradeoff and nonpreemptible regain delay.
Reviewed queue stability and no-universal-partition limits.
proof_review.notes: No formal proof of a concrete scheduler, database, container/cell, security property or safety case is claimed.

evidence: Audited isolated, independent, reserved, bounded, fair, critical, stable, safe, guarantee and proof language.
Confirmed conditional resource proofs, deterministic accounting, empirical load/fault evidence and external human review are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter explicitly names residual shared resources as limits on blast-radius claims.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/SEPAT-084/report.json
Reproduced allocation sum, budget comparison and independent fixed-limit admission outputs using Python 3.
Confirmed the model performs no concurrency, queues, release, I/O, resource allocation or fault injection.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes static arithmetic only; its isolation label is not a live containment experiment.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats Bulkhead as multidimensional resource/failure containment with explicit residual coupling, not merely separate executor names.

practitioner_review.notes: Guidance covers resource/failure graphs, capacity derivation, semaphore/executor/queue/process/cell options, permit lifecycle, priority/fairness/borrowing, composition, telemetry, shutdown and containment tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: Objectives align with conditional proofs, deterministic allocation trace, ten distinct cases and five exercises progressing from design through multidimensional arithmetic, capacity reasoning, diagnosis and safety-critical judgment.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
